b: When it’s Christmastime, there are a few movies I like to watch year after year. One of those is Elf. It’s not only one of my favorite Christmas movies, but one of my favorite movies in general.

So to kick off the Christmas season, today I talk with Andy Richter. Andy played Morris, who works at Walter Hobbs’ publishing house in the film. He’s also the co-author of a new book on the making of the movie, Elf Unwrapped.

Today on the show, Andy takes us behind the scenes of how Elf went from a script that bounced around Hollywood for years to a modern Christmas classic. We discuss how Will Ferrell and Jon Favreau got attached to the project, the two contrasting elements their competing visions generated that gave the movie its special alchemy, the unpredictable nature of creative success, and the improvisation and practical effects behind Elf ‘s distinctive charm. We talk both about fun facts, like who else was considered to play Buddy besides Will Ferrell and whether the snow in the Central Park snowball fight was real, and get to the bottom of why Elf continues to resonate with audiences more than two decades after its release and what it says about the human desire for magic.
